title: Building an open ETL tool to convert archived .nrd Market Replay files to Parquet/CSV - Looking to pool historical NQ/ES files (2022–2025)
author: Illegalyfaty

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the 90 day purge is brutal, this is useful. worth stamping each file with which data connection recorded it, since replays from different feeds can disagree on tick timestamps, and pooled files from several people will mix them silently.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: cheers, good luck with the pooling.

replies.author: Illegalyfaty
replies.body:
Went back and checked my code and you made a great point. Mixing timestamps from different feeds (like Rithmic vs CQG) would cause subtle microsecond desyncs that are a nightmare to debug later.

I just updated the pipeline to embed data\_feed / provider tags directly into the Parquet metadata so every file stays segregated by its original data source.

Thanks for the insight! By the way, do you happen to have any archived data sitting on your drives? I didn't emphasize it enough in the post, but the pipeline actually supports a lot more than just NinjaTrader8 it can now ingest feeds from Sierra Chart (.depth/.scid), Bookmap (.bmf), Quantower, or raw broker tick dumps. (for now only those)

If you have older NQ or ES archives in any format and want them converted to clean Parquet with all the order book stats, I'd be more than happy to process them for you.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: nice, the parquet metadata is the right home for it since it travels with the file. if you ever merge feeds, keep the exchange timestamp and your receive time as two separate columns, collapsing them is where the microsecond mess usually comes back.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Tagging the data feed in the metadata is a good fix. I'd also record the time zone and the clock source for each timestamp (exchange time versus receive time), and a hash for each file with the conversion code version, so pooled data can be traced and re-run later. If a file has gaps or session breaks, a small quality report next to it (missing intervals, out-of-order ticks) will save others a lot of debugging. Events like CPI and FOMC create sudden depth changes in that kind of data, and Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for macro releases) is one source for flagging those windows.
